new.n: Iron Exchange Bank loot, Hurley: $39,000 said buried or sunk in the Montreal River
new.pl: Hurley village point; the 1895 theory says 'some point north of Hurley' on the Montreal River, which runs north from the town to Lake Superior. Pin is the town, not a spot.
new.st: On the night of Friday 20 September 1889 nearly $40,000 of express-company money was taken from the vault of the Iron Exchange Bank at Hurley, opened with the combination. It was an inside job: in November 1889 the bank's bookkeeper and an Ironwood saloonkeeper were arrested; the saloonkeeper was convicted at Ashland in June 1890 and served five years at Waupun. The amount was put at $39,000 and only about $1,100 was ever recovered. When he was released in April 1895 the Marinette Eagle reported the detectives' belief that the money had been carried to some point north of Hurley and buried, or sunk in a watertight box in the Montreal River; a Duluth paper the same week said buried in Ashland or Iron County or sunk in the river. No find was ever reported.
new.t: Lead grade D: the robbery, conviction and $1,100 recovery are period record, but where the rest went is one 1895 detective theory. The Montreal River north of Hurley is the state line through county forest and private land; look only, and diving or digging needs permission.
src: Neenah Daily Times, 18 Apr 1895, p. 4, quoting the Marinette Eagle (Newspapers.com 444919651)
pinev: Pin on Hurley (same point as the Hurley saloons card) 46.4499,-90.1809, r5000; the 1895 theory names no place closer than 'north of Hurley'.
new.tovw: Lead grade D: period papers confirm the 1889 theft and that about $37,900 was never recovered; the burial or river-box story rests on a single 1895 detectives' theory reprinted by two papers, with no place closer than 'north of Hurley'
